titulo: Shopping, clothes, colours, este and ese: Este, ese and aquel

aula.titulo: Shopping, clothes, colours, este and ese
aula.objetivo: Name clothes and colors with the right agreement, ask about prices and sizes, pay, use the numbers 100 to 1000, point at objects with este, ese and aquel, and handle a short purchase in a store.

blocos.titulo: The demonstratives: este, ese, and aquel
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: demonstratives point at something and signal distance. «Este» is for what's near the speaker; «ese» is for what's near the listener or a bit further away; «aquel» is for what's far from both. They pair with «aquí, ahí, allí». STEP 2: the forms of «este»: este, esta, estos, estas. Of «ese»: ese, esa, esos, esas. Of «aquel»: aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas. STEP 3: the demonstrative agrees with the noun in gender and number and comes before it: «esta camisa», «ese abrigo», «aquellos zapatos». STEP 4: without the noun, the demonstrative works as a pronoun: «Quiero este» (I want this one), «¿Cuánto cuesta esa?» (how much does that one cost?). Today it's written with no accent mark. STEP 5: «esto», «eso» and «aquello» are neuter: they're for an unidentified thing or an idea, and they never change form: «¿Qué es esto?» (what's this?), «Eso es caro» (that's expensive). STEP 6: there's no fusion with a preposition: «in this» is «en este», «of/from this» is «de esta», «in that» is «en ese». STEP 7: to choose between two things: «¿Cuál prefieres: este o ese?» (which do you prefer, this one or that one?) — lesson 16 covers more of this.
blocos.comparacao: English also has this near/far distinction, but collapses it into just two words, «this» and «that», where Spanish keeps three levels of distance (este/ese/aquel) tied to speaker, listener, and neither. And where English happily fuses a preposition straight onto the demonstrative-adjacent phrase («in this store»), Spanish never fuses the preposition onto the demonstrative itself: it's always «en esta tienda», never a contracted form, and «of that coat» is «de ese abrigo», word for word, with no shortcut.

exemplos.pt: Those shoes over there are cheap.

tabela.distancia: [misto] near you, or a bit further (ahí)

erros.motivo: «Pantalones» is plural, and so is the verb.
For something you don't know the identity of, use the neuter «esto».
With no preposition, the demonstrative just points at the object.

blocos.titulo: En la tienda / At the store
blocos.contexto: Lucía is buying a jacket; the sales assistant helps her.

linhas.pt: — Good afternoon. What would you like?

linhas.ru: — Buenas tardes. Busco una chaqueta negra.
linhas.pt: — Good afternoon. I'm looking for a black jacket.
linhas.audio: Buenas tardes. Busco una chaqueta negra.

linhas.ru: — Tenemos estas dos. Esta es de algodón y esa es de lana.
linhas.pt: — We have these two. This one is cotton and that one is wool.
linhas.audio: Tenemos estas dos. Esta es de algodón y esa es de lana.

linhas.pt: — That's a bit pricey. And that one?

linhas.ru: — Esa cuesta cuarenta euros y está en rebajas.
linhas.pt: — That one costs forty euros and it's on sale.
linhas.audio: Esa cuesta cuarenta euros y está en rebajas.

linhas.pt: — Perfect. Can I try on this jacket?

linhas.ru: — Claro. El probador está al fondo.
linhas.pt: — Of course. The fitting room is at the back.
linhas.audio: Claro. El probador está al fondo.

linhas.ru: — Me queda bien. Quiero esta chaqueta.
linhas.pt: — It fit me well. I'll take this jacket.
linhas.audio: Me queda bien. Quiero esta chaqueta.

linhas.pt: — Are you paying by card or in cash?

blocos.enunciado: Pick two objects in your house, one near and one far, and say: «Este… es… Aquel… es… ¿Cuánto cuesta ese?». Use a color in each sentence.
Say the prices of three items in euros: «Cuesta treinta y cinco euros… ciento veinte euros…»
